collection.name: Second Nature: Documentary Screening with Dame Judi Dentures & Friends
collection.support: Film Screening + Drag Performances + Reception with Local Queer and Trans Organizations
collection.description:
Second Nature: Documenting Queer Gender and Sexuality in the Animal World

A Documentary Produced and Narrated by Elliot Page

Sunday, November 29 4-6:30pm

The Rooted Co-op and Dame Judi Dentures Productions present a free community screening of Second Nature, Elliot Page’s funny, heartwarming documentary about queer and trans diversity in the animal world. The afternoon will begin with drag performances by Dame Judi Dentures and other local artists, followed by the film screening, and then a reception with resource tables from local LGBTQ+-affirming organizations including TransHealth and Translate Gender. Sliding scale tickets (with a free option!) support event costs and free screenings of the film for LGBTQIA+ youth in states where inclusive sex ed is banned. All are welcome. We highly recommend reserving a spot in advance, as capacity is limited. Reserve your spot here.

collection.name: CitySpace 20th Anniversary Celebration
collection.description:
Thursday, December 3, 2026 | 6–9 pm
CitySpace at Old Town Hall, 43 Main Street, Easthampton

Celebrate 20 years of CitySpace at Future Forward, a one-night-only, pull-out-all-the-stops celebration of Old Town Hall’s past, present, and very big future.

Expect delectable food, music by DJ Bex Taylor, the incomparable Dame Judi Denchers as emcee, live entertainment, fabulous auction items, raffles, surprises, and plenty of reasons to raise a glass. We’re celebrating two decades of artists, performances, wild ideas, community, and the people who helped transform a historic building into a place where magical and creative things happen.

Twenty years deserves a party. This is that party.

We are grateful to the businesses and organizations who are making Future Forward possible including Chemetal,  KW Home and Galaxy.   

Sliding scale tickets are available starting at $35 ($37.13 with fees). All ticket levels include admission and food. Choose the level that works for you, or give a little more to help support. CitySpace and what comes next.

Cash bar available. Festive attire inspired by the past, present, or future is encouraged (not required).

collection.name: Haley Kean - Passive Forms
collection.description:
Haley Kean - Passive Forms

December 5, 2026 - December 23 , 2026

Art Walk and Artist reception: Saturday, December 5, 4-7pm

Exhibition Statement: In Passive Forms, I explore the relationship between my hometown of Newtown CT, and the abandoned institution of Fairfield Hills. Drawing inspiration from Hokusai’s 36 Views of Mount Fuji Series, I created this body of work to illuminate the location that the people of Newtown live their daily lives around. The campus has been collectively reimagined as an active participant in the social ecology of Newtown; It has become a wayfinding device, a projection of self and community. In my work, I interpret space within Fairfield Hills, while emulating the visceral atmosphere of a place with layered identity. I do so through scale and detail within the etchings, juxtaposed with the spontaneous materiality of the plaster-casting process. I focus the project with large scale drawings that become abstracted vignettes of place and time on the site of Fairfield Hills.

Bio: Haley Kean is an artist based in Northampton, MA. They received their MFA in Printmaking from Ohio University, and BFA in Studio Art from Keene State College. Kean works with space, and narrative tools to visually interpret the radical compassion of the human experience, attachment, and grief.

collection.name: CitySpace Bluegrass
collection.description:
Join bluegrass musician David Clark Carroll and CitySpace for a fun, open bluegrass jam! Bring your instruments and your favorite tunes — from Bill Monroe to the Stanley Brothers and beyond. Held every first Saturday of the month during Art Walk Easthampton, this monthly jam brings the community together for music, connection, and good old-fashioned fun.

All are welcome. Free to join. All ages.

About David Clark Carroll

David Clark Carroll is a powerhouse bluegrass musician and the founder of Daring Coyotes, a progressive bluegrass band known for captivating performances across New England. Before returning east, David was a prominent bluegrass musician in Nevada City, CA, where he performed with multiple bands, hosted jams, and served as a regional director for the California Bluegrass Association. Known for his dynamic performances, David continues to play solo and with his string band, captivating audiences with his unique sound.

CitySpace Bluegrass is made possible by the Community Foundation of Western Massachusetts, Massachusetts Cultural Council,TruNorth Bank, Keiter, USA Waste & Recycle, and Big E’s Supermarket. Thank you for your support!

collection.name: CitySpace Presents: Stories I Haven't Heard
collection.description:
Stories I Haven’t Heard

Sung by Leo Harrison & Friends

December 11

Pay it Forward 2026

After many years of feeling more comfortable behind the scenes, Leo is returning to performance as a means of voicing stories that have never been heard before. In pursuing ancestral connections, he feels drawn to imagine the lives of those who came before us, reclaim the songs that were stolen and lost, and maybe embellish the truth a little. Leo’s music conjures modern folktales, forgotten legends, and everything in between.

Leo Harrison

A gifted jazz vocalist, Leo Harrison (he/him) croons over syncopated bass lines, colorful keys, and hip hop beats with supreme ease. His cool, sophisticated musicality is reminiscent of Stevie Wonder and João Gilberto, not only in ingenuity but in his ability to convey complex ideas in deceptively palatable ways. This ability is more than a knack, it’s a means of survival. As an autistic trans man, Leo has to swim upstream, and his music is rife with Black American blues. Yet Leo perseveres, and his songs of love and everlasting comfort shine all the brighter.

Pay It Forward events are made possible by the Community Foundation of Western Mass, Massachusetts Cultural Council, Greenfield Savings Bank, Never Give Up, Greenfield Northampton Cooperative Bank, Tom Schiff Consulting, Tandem Bagel Company and Waugh Agency Insurance.

collection.name: CitySpace Presents: Scott Hsu Album Release Show
collection.description:
Scott Hsu, December 12

Pay it Forward 2026

album release show

Scott Hsu, is a Taiwanese-American rock/pop/electronica artist from Amherst Massachusetts. His songs are passionate and heartfelt, rooted in authenticity, gravitating toward themes of love, nostalgia, transformation, and redemption. With lyrics in English and Mandarin, he blends his cross-cultural heritage into his music to reflect his unique identity—global, hybrid, and personal. Scott’s latest singles include the dreamy Chinglish pop/punk song "陪你 / I Just Wanna Be With You" (2025) and the plucky pop Americana tune "You Got My Love" (2024). His discography includes his acoustic album Confessional EP (2025), and Cliffs EP (2024), which features the catchy synth rock single "Play"

Children under 12 get in for free

collection.name: CitySpace Presents: Foes of a Minimum Wage Guard
collection.description:
Foes of a Minimum Wage Guard- A Solo Play, January 8 & 9

Pay it Forward

Foes of a Minimum Wage Guard is an award-winning solo comedy-drama play in which a 68-year-old retail worker is suddenly reassigned to loss prevention without training and must protect a struggling department store—or risk losing his job. Performed by Ken Harris portraying 12 different characters, the play explores workplace pressure, resilience, and the search for dignity through humor, suspense, and heartfelt storytelling.

Ken Harris

Ken Harris is a Springfield, Massachusetts-based playwright, actor, filmmaker, and solo performer whose work explores themes of resilience, social justice, and the experiences of everyday people. He is the creator and performer of Foes of a Minimum Wage Guard, an original one-man play portraying twelve characters and examining workplace discrimination, economic insecurity, and personal dignity through the story of an aging retail worker. Harris has performed the play throughout Massachusetts, Connecticut, and New York, including at the United Solo Theatre Festival in New York City. His work has been supported by the Springfield, Chicopee, and Agawam Cultural Councils, and he is a member of the Springfield Cultural Partnership Cohort. In 2026, Harris received the Mass Indie Spirit Award for his short film The Phantom Ruse. Through theater and film, he is committed to creating engaging, community-centered stories that inspire conversation, reflection, and connection.

Pay It Forward events are made possible by the Community Foundation of Western Mass, Massachusetts Cultural Council, Greenfield Savings Bank, Never Give Up, Greenfield Northampton Cooperative Bank, Tom Schiff Consulting, Tandem Bagel Company and Waugh Agency Insurance.

collection.name: CitySpace Presents: Late Night with the Public Domain
collection.description:
Late Night with the Public Domain, January 29 & 30

Pay it Forward

Late Night with the Public Domain; a late night talk show where expired IPs take the stage. Part talent show, part comedy sketch with  puppets, singing, dancing, hand constructed wild sets and more.

Ang Buxton mentored Bella Levavi, performing stand up comedy and producing an array of shows, they are back on stage with a big weird show. Ang recently performed at the We Make Noise Festival and is the founder of Far Out Fest. Bella is a puppeteer, she organizes Greenfield Crankie Fest.
